newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Royal Caribbean to buy Celebrity.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Royal Caribbean to buy Celebrity.

text.p: Royal Caribbean International said Tuesday it will pay $230 million in cash and issue 7.4 million shares of stock for Celebrity Cruise Lines Inc. The transaction will result in a fleet of 20 ships by the year 2000.
A full text of the company's press release follows.

MIAMI, June 17 /PRNewswire/ -- Royal Caribbean International (NYSE: RCL) and Celebrity Cruise Lines Inc., an equal joint venture between the Chandris Group and Overseas Shipholding Group, Inc. (NYSE: OSG), announced today the signing of an agreement to merge the two companies. The value of the transaction is $1.3 billion and, between the two brands, will result in an overall fleet of 20 ships, totaling over 38,000 berths by the year 2000. These totals include five vessels currently on order. The purchase is subject to certain conditions precedent, including due diligence, board approvals and definitive agreements.

"Strategically, this combination helps reshape the vacation industry landscape by providing each brand with the market presence and the operating strengths of the other," said Richard D. Fain, Royal Caribbean's chairman and CEO. "The addition of the Celebrity brand, long recognized for its outstanding service and premium attractions, coupled with five excellent vessels and a strong management team, will further reinforce Royal Caribbean's leadership in the cruise industry. I'm pleased to announce that John Chandris has agreed to stay on as chairman of Celebrity for the time being.
"Together, the two brands will enable us to deploy vessels and attract customers on an increasingly global basis, as well as provide opportunities to achieve greater economies of scale," Fain added.
Royal Caribbean intends to maintain the Celebrity brand separate from the Royal Caribbean brand, allowing each to maximize its respective brand strengths within its own category.

"The dynamics of the marketplace and the cruise industry require brand expansion and strategic alliances that emphasize growth strategies," said John Chandris. "The combined experience of our cruise vacation companies is unparalleled. Their brand awareness and market presence will offer the cruising public the youngest fleet and most diverse product serving the broadest spectrum of worldwide destinations."

The total transaction calls for a purchase price for the equity of approximately $500 million and the assumption of approximately $800 million in debt. The purchase price will be paid by a combination of $230 million in cash and the issuance of 7.4 million shares of Royal Caribbean common stock. The company intends to utilize existing and/or new credit lines to finance the cash portion of the purchase price. The company contemplates, subsequent to the completion of the transaction, issuing additional common stock to finance the cash portion of the purchase price. The company expects some dilution in earnings per share for 1998 and accretion thereafter.

Including the delivery of Mercury this October, Celebrity will operate five ships with a double occupancy capacity of 8,200 berths. All of these ships will have been built in the 1990s. The line sails throughout Alaska, Bermuda, the Caribbean and the Panama Canal.

Royal Caribbean operates 11 ships with a total capacity of 19,770. It has four new ships on order, including two 130,000-ton Eagle-class vessels scheduled for service beginning in 1999. The company offers 66 itineraries and 156 destinations in Alaska, the Bahamas, Bermuda, the Caribbean, Europe, the Far East, Hawaii, Mexico, Panama Canal, Russia and Scandinavia.
